title: Fat Loss — Mediterranean
summary: The Mediterranean diet is one of the most research-backed approaches to sustainable fat loss. High in vegetables, lean protein, healthy fats, and fibre. Naturally portion-friendly because whole foods are filling. The goal is a 300-500 calorie daily deficit through food quality and portion control — not starvation.
calories: Calculate your TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) and subtract 400 calories. This is your daily target. Weigh yourself weekly — if losing more than 1.5 lbs/week, eat 200 more calories. If losing nothing after 2 weeks, cut another 100.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: 30-35% of calories (mostly olive oil, fish, nuts). Carbs: fill the rest — prioritise vegetables, legumes, and whole grains.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 2 eggs scrambled in 1 tsp olive oil + 1 cup spinach + 1 slice whole grain toast
• OR Greek yoghurt (plain, full fat) + handful of berries + 1 tbsp walnuts
• Black coffee or herbal tea

LUNCH
• Large salad: mixed greens + cucumber + tomato + olives + chickpeas (½ cup) + 4oz grilled chicken or tuna + 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon
• OR lentil soup (1.5 cups) + side salad

DINNER
• 5oz grilled salmon or white fish + roasted vegetables (zucchini, peppers, eggplant) + ½ cup quinoa or brown rice
• OR chicken thigh (baked) + large plate of roasted vegetables + small amount of hummus

SNACKS (pick 1-2 per day)
• Handful of almonds or walnuts (measured — 1oz)
• Cucumber + 2 tbsp hummus
• Apple + 1 tbsp almond butter
• Hard boiled egg
portion_control: Use a 9-inch plate. Half the plate is vegetables. One quarter is protein. One quarter is whole grains or legumes. Olive oil is healthy but calorie-dense — measure it, don't pour. Nuts are easy to overeat — pre-portion them.
struggle_tips:
CRAVINGS: The Mediterranean diet handles cravings well because fat and fibre keep you full. If cravings hit, drink water first — thirst mimics hunger. Dark chocolate (1-2 squares) is on plan.
PORTION CONTROL: Eat slowly. Put the fork down between bites. Stop at 80% full — it takes 20 minutes for satiety signals to reach your brain.
CONSISTENCY: Prep your lunch the night before. Decision fatigue kills diets — having food ready removes the choice.
foods_to_avoid: Refined carbs (white bread, pastries), processed meats, sugary drinks, seed oils, fast food, alcohol (or limit to 1 glass of red wine occasionally).

title: Fat Loss — Keto
summary: Ketogenic fat loss works by switching your primary fuel source from carbohydrates to fat. When carbs drop below 20-30g per day, your body enters ketosis and begins burning stored body fat efficiently. Hunger is naturally reduced in ketosis — use this to your advantage with portion control.
calories: Subtract 400-500 calories from your TDEE. Keto has a natural appetite-suppressing effect — most people find portion control easier once fat-adapted (2-4 weeks in). Don't track obsessively at first — focus on eliminating carbs. Then dial in calories if fat loss stalls.
macros: Fat: 65-75% of calories. Protein: 0.8g per lb of bodyweight. Carbs: under 25g net per day — this is non-negotiable. Net carbs = total carbs minus fibre.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3 eggs scrambled in butter + 2 strips bacon + ½ avocado
• OR bulletproof coffee (black coffee + 1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp MCT oil, blended) if intermittent fasting

LUNCH
• 5oz ground beef or chicken thigh cooked in butter + large salad (greens, cucumber, avocado, olive oil dressing)
• OR tuna salad (canned tuna + mayo + celery) on lettuce wraps

DINNER
• 6oz ribeye or salmon + roasted broccoli or cauliflower in butter or olive oil + side salad
• OR chicken thighs (skin on, baked) + sautéed spinach + creamy cauliflower mash

SNACKS (pick 1 if hungry)
• Cheese (1-2oz)
• Hard boiled eggs (1-2)
• Handful of macadamia nuts or pecans
• Celery + almond butter (1 tbsp)
portion_control: Protein portions matter on keto — too much protein converts to glucose via gluconeogenesis and can slow ketosis. Stick to 4-6oz protein per meal. Fat is filling — don't force extra fat if not hungry. Eat to satiety, not beyond it.
struggle_tips:
KETO FLU (week 1-2): Headaches and fatigue are normal as your body adapts. Salt your food liberally, drink bone broth, and supplement magnesium and potassium.
CRAVINGS: Sugar cravings peak in week 1-2 then drop significantly. Push through — ketosis kills sugar addiction.
EATING OUT: Steak and salad, burger without the bun, grilled fish with vegetables. Most restaurants can accommodate keto if you ask.
foods_to_avoid: All grains (bread, pasta, rice, oats), sugar and sweeteners, most fruit, legumes, starchy vegetables (potato, corn, peas), beer, most alcohol, low-fat dairy products.

title: Fat Loss — Carnivore
summary: The carnivore diet eliminates everything except animal products. It is highly satiating, eliminates food decisions, and naturally creates a calorie deficit for most people through protein's high thermic effect and extreme satiety. Simple, strict, and effective for those who commit to it.
calories: Most carnivore dieters don't count calories — protein and fat are so satiating that overeating is difficult. However for deliberate fat loss, aim for 400 calories below TDEE. If fat loss stalls after 3 weeks, reduce fat intake slightly (lean more on lean cuts rather than fatty ones).
macros: Protein: 1-1.2g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: the remainder of your calories. Carbs: zero. The ratio of protein to fat determines your deficit — leaner cuts = lower calories.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3-4 eggs cooked in butter + 3 strips bacon
• OR 6oz ground beef patty (80/20) pan-fried in its own fat
• Black coffee (some carnivore dieters include this, others don't)

LUNCH
• 6oz chicken thighs or breast (skin on) + 2 hard boiled eggs
• OR canned sardines or salmon + 2-3 slices deli turkey or beef

DINNER
• 8oz ribeye, NY strip, or sirloin, cooked in butter
• OR 8oz salmon or other fatty fish
• OR ground beef (6oz) + lamb chops

SNACKS (only if genuinely hungry)
• Hard boiled eggs
• Beef jerky (no sugar added)
• Cheese (if tolerating dairy)
• Sliced deli meat
portion_control: Eat when hungry, stop when full. Carnivore is unique in that satiety signals are very clear — protein and fat together trigger strong fullness hormones. Don't eat out of habit or boredom. For faster fat loss, choose leaner cuts at dinner (sirloin over ribeye, chicken breast over thigh).
struggle_tips:
ADAPTATION (week 1-3): Fatigue, digestive changes, and cravings are normal. Salt heavily, stay hydrated, and push through. Most people feel significantly better by week 3.
SOCIAL EATING: Steak, burger patty, eggs, and bacon exist on almost every menu. Order confidently.
CONSTIPATION: Common early on. Drink more water. This typically resolves within 2-3 weeks as the gut adapts.
foods_to_avoid: Everything that isn't an animal product — all plants, grains, vegetables, fruit, seed oils, sugar, and processed foods. Some carnivore dieters include dairy; others exclude it. If fat loss stalls, cut dairy first.

title: Fat Loss — Vegetarian
summary: Vegetarian fat loss requires deliberate protein focus — the biggest pitfall is replacing meat with high-carb fillers that stall fat loss. Build every meal around a protein source first, then add vegetables, then a small amount of complex carbs. Portion control is critical because plant-based carbs are easy to overeat.
calories: Subtract 400 calories from your TDEE. Vegetarian diets can be high in calories from carbs and oils without feeling like it — tracking for the first 2-3 weeks is strongly recommended to calibrate.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb of bodyweight — this requires intention on a vegetarian diet. Fat: 25-30% of calories. Carbs: the remainder, prioritising high-fibre options.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3 egg omelette with spinach, mushrooms, and feta + ½ slice whole grain toast
• OR Greek yoghurt (plain) + ½ cup berries + 2 tbsp hemp seeds
• OR cottage cheese (½ cup) + apple slices

LUNCH
• Large salad: mixed greens + chickpeas (½ cup) + hard boiled egg + cucumber + 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon
• OR lentil soup (1.5 cups) + side of Greek yoghurt
• OR tofu stir-fry (5oz firm tofu) + lots of vegetables + 2 tbsp soy sauce, served over ½ cup brown rice

DINNER
• Tempeh (5oz) pan-fried with vegetables + small portion of quinoa
• OR black bean tacos (corn tortillas, 2 small) + lots of salsa, lettuce, and hot sauce
• OR vegetable curry with chickpeas + ½ cup brown rice

SNACKS
• Cottage cheese (½ cup)
• Hard boiled eggs (1-2)
• Edamame (½ cup)
• Apple + 1 tbsp almond butter
portion_control: Grains and legumes are healthy but calorie-dense — measure them until you have a feel for correct portions. ½ cup cooked grains is a serving, not 2 cups. Cheese adds up fast — weigh it. Load the plate with vegetables first, then add protein, then add a small scoop of carbs.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN: Aim for 25-30g protein per meal. Greek yoghurt, eggs, cottage cheese, tofu, tempeh, and legumes are your main tools. Don't rely solely on legumes — the carbs add up.
CRAVINGS: High-fibre vegetables and protein at every meal reduce cravings significantly. If sweet cravings hit, Greek yoghurt with berries handles it without breaking the plan.
EATING OUT: Ask for extra vegetables, choose egg-based dishes, lentil soups, or tofu options. Avoid pasta-heavy dishes.
foods_to_avoid: White bread, pastries, sugary drinks, processed vegetarian meat replacements (most are high in sodium and refined carbs), excessive cheese, fried foods, alcohol.

title: Fat Loss — Vegan
summary: Vegan fat loss is absolutely achievable but requires the most nutritional planning of any dietary style. Protein is the biggest challenge — it must be deliberately built into every meal. Whole food plant-based eating is naturally high in fibre and volume, which helps with satiety and portion control.
calories: Subtract 400 calories from TDEE. Vegan diets can be surprisingly calorie-dense (nuts, nut butters, avocado, oils) — track for 2 weeks to calibrate. The goal is high volume, high fibre, and high protein within the calorie target.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb of bodyweight — requires serious intention on a vegan diet. Fat: 20-25% of calories. Carbs: the rest — prioritise legumes, vegetables, and whole grains over refined carbs.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Tofu scramble (5oz firm tofu crumbled + turmeric + nutritional yeast + spinach + peppers)
• OR protein smoothie: plant protein powder (25g protein) + almond milk + banana + spinach + 1 tbsp flaxseed
• OR overnight oats: ½ cup oats + almond milk + 2 tbsp hemp seeds + berries

LUNCH
• Large salad: mixed greens + 1 cup chickpeas or black beans + avocado (¼) + cucumber + tahini dressing (1 tbsp)
• OR lentil soup (2 cups) + 2 rye crispbreads
• OR tempeh bowl (5oz) + roasted vegetables + ½ cup quinoa + soy sauce

DINNER
• Tofu stir-fry (6oz firm tofu) + large portion of mixed vegetables + ½ cup brown rice
• OR black bean chilli (large bowl) + small corn tortilla
• OR chickpea and vegetable curry + ½ cup basmati rice

SNACKS
• Edamame (½ cup)
• Roasted chickpeas
• Apple + 1 tbsp almond butter
• Vegan protein bar (check sugar content)
portion_control: Nuts, nut butters, avocado, and oils are calorie-dense — measure them every time. Legumes are your protein backbone but also contain carbs — account for them. Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables at every meal before adding anything else.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN: This is the hardest part of vegan fat loss. Tofu, tempeh, edamame, seitan, and legumes at every meal. A plant-based protein powder is strongly recommended to hit targets without extra carbs.
B12 AND IRON: Supplement B12. Eat iron-rich plant foods (lentils, spinach, tofu) with vitamin C to improve absorption.
EATING OUT: Thai, Indian, and Middle Eastern restaurants have the best vegan options. Ask for tofu or extra legumes.
foods_to_avoid: All animal products, refined grains, sugary drinks, processed vegan junk food (vegan cheese, vegan desserts, packaged snacks), excessive oils, white rice and white bread.

title: Fat Loss — Paleo
summary: Paleo fat loss eliminates processed foods, grains, legumes, and dairy — and replaces them with meat, fish, eggs, vegetables, fruit, nuts, and seeds. The elimination of processed carbs and sugar naturally reduces calorie intake for most people. Portion control focuses on protein and vegetables as the foundation of every meal.
calories: Subtract 400 calories from TDEE. Paleo naturally reduces calorie intake by eliminating high-calorie processed foods. If fat loss stalls, reduce fruit and nut intake first — these are the easiest sources of hidden calories on paleo.
macros: Protein: 0.85g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: 30-40% of calories (from meat, fish, eggs, avocado, nuts). Carbs: the rest — from vegetables and limited fruit only.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3 eggs scrambled + ½ avocado + handful of spinach cooked in coconut oil
• OR sweet potato hash: diced sweet potato (½ cup) + ground turkey + peppers + onion
• Black coffee (no dairy)

LUNCH
• Large salad: mixed greens + 5oz grilled chicken or tuna + avocado (¼) + cucumber + olive oil + lemon
• OR lettuce wrap tacos: ground beef + salsa + avocado + lettuce cups

DINNER
• 6oz salmon or other fish + large plate of roasted vegetables (broccoli, zucchini, peppers, asparagus)
• OR grass-fed beef patty + roasted sweet potato (small) + side salad
• OR chicken thighs (baked) + cauliflower rice + roasted carrots

SNACKS
• Hard boiled eggs (1-2)
• Apple + handful of almonds
• Beef jerky (no sugar, no nitrates)
• Celery + almond butter (1 tbsp)
portion_control: Paleo is naturally portion-friendly because whole foods are filling. The main overeating traps are nuts (easy to eat a handful too many) and fruit (natural sugar adds up). Measure nuts to 1oz. Limit fruit to 1-2 pieces per day on a fat loss phase. Protein and vegetables are essentially unlimited — lean on them.
struggle_tips:
EATING OUT: Grilled meat or fish + vegetables + salad fits paleo at almost any restaurant. Ask for no grains, no sauces (most contain sugar or soy).
SNACK CRAVINGS: Paleo-compliant snacks still have calories. If you're snacking heavily, eat more protein at meals — hunger between meals usually means not enough protein at the previous meal.
MEAL PREP: Paleo works best when food is prepared in advance. Batch cook protein on Sunday — chicken, ground beef, hard boiled eggs.
foods_to_avoid: Grains (bread, pasta, rice, oats), legumes (beans, peanuts, soy), dairy, refined sugar, processed foods, seed oils (canola, soybean, sunflower), alcohol, artificial sweeteners.

title: Fat Loss — Intermittent Fasting
summary: Intermittent fasting creates a calorie deficit by compressing your eating window. The most popular protocol is 16:8 — fast for 16 hours, eat within an 8-hour window. Fat loss happens because you naturally eat fewer calories when you have less time to eat. What you eat within the window still matters enormously.
calories: Subtract 400-500 calories from TDEE. Spread across your eating window — typically 2-3 meals. Don't try to eat all your normal day's food in a shorter window — the point is to eat less overall.
macros: Protein: 0.85g per lb of bodyweight — critical to prioritise at every meal since you have fewer of them. Fat: 30% of calories. Carbs: the rest, timed around your workout if you train.
meals:
EATING WINDOW EXAMPLE: 12pm – 8pm (16:8 protocol)

MEAL 1 (12pm — break fast)
• Large meal: 6oz chicken breast or salmon + large salad or roasted vegetables + ½ cup brown rice or sweet potato
• This meal should be your largest — you're breaking an overnight fast

MEAL 2 (4pm — mid-window)
• 5oz protein (any source) + vegetables + small amount of complex carbs
• OR high-protein snack: Greek yoghurt + protein shake + fruit

MEAL 3 (7:30pm — close to window close)
• 5-6oz protein + large portion of vegetables + healthy fat
• Keep this meal lower in carbs — you're approaching the fast

DURING THE FAST
• Black coffee, plain tea, sparkling water — all acceptable
• Nothing with calories. Even small amounts break the metabolic benefits of fasting.
portion_control: With fewer meals, each one needs to be nutritionally complete. Don't skip vegetables to fit more protein — fibre keeps you full during the fast. The danger zone is breaking the fast with high-calorie, low-nutrition food — you're hungry and will overeat junk if it's available. Have your first meal ready.
struggle_tips:
HUNGER DURING FAST: Peaks around 8-10am then typically subsides. Black coffee suppresses appetite significantly. Stay busy during morning hours.
SLEEP AND FASTING: Your sleeping hours count toward your fast — a 10pm-6am sleep means you only need to fast 6 more hours to hit 16. Much more manageable.
SOCIAL EATING: Adjust your window for social situations — shift to 1pm-9pm on dinner-out days. Flexibility is sustainable.
foods_to_avoid: Within your window: sugary drinks, ultra-processed food, refined carbs, alcohol (breaks the fast and adds empty calories). During fasting window: anything with calories.

title: Fat Loss — Gluten-Free
summary: Gluten-free fat loss focuses on naturally gluten-free whole foods — rice, potatoes, meat, fish, eggs, vegetables, and fruit. The trap is gluten-free processed products — they are often higher in sugar and calories than their regular counterparts. Real food, not gluten-free substitutes, is the strategy.
calories: Subtract 400 calories from TDEE. Avoid gluten-free bread, pasta, and baked goods — they are calorie-dense and often spike blood sugar more than regular versions. Build meals from naturally gluten-free whole foods instead.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: 30% of calories. Carbs: from rice, potatoes, vegetables, fruit, and legumes — not gluten-free packaged products.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3 eggs scrambled + vegetables + ½ cup cooked rice or 1 small potato (roasted)
• OR Greek yoghurt + berries + 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds
• OR smoothie: banana + spinach + protein powder (check label — GF) + almond milk

LUNCH
• 5oz grilled chicken or fish + large salad (naturally GF dressing: olive oil + lemon)
• OR rice bowl: ½ cup brown rice + 5oz protein + roasted vegetables + tamari (GF soy sauce)
• OR lentil soup + side salad

DINNER
• 6oz salmon or chicken + roasted potatoes (small) + large plate of roasted vegetables
• OR ground turkey stir-fry + rice noodles (100g) + vegetables + tamari
• OR steak + sweet potato + salad

SNACKS
• Rice cakes (2) + almond butter
• Hard boiled eggs
• Fruit + nuts (1oz)
• Edamame
portion_control: Rice and potatoes are the primary carb sources — measure them (½ cup cooked rice, 1 medium potato). Gluten-free crackers and snack foods are easy to overeat — pre-portion them or avoid entirely. Protein and vegetables have no meaningful portion restriction — fill up on them.
struggle_tips:
LABEL READING: Gluten hides in sauces, marinades, dressings, and seasonings. Use tamari instead of soy sauce. Make your own sauces when possible.
EATING OUT: Most restaurants can accommodate GF — grilled protein + vegetables + rice is available almost everywhere. Ask about cross-contamination if coeliac.
GLUTEN-FREE JUNK FOOD: GF cookies, bread, and pasta are not health food. They're often worse for fat loss than their regular counterparts. Avoid them.
foods_to_avoid: All wheat, barley, rye, and regular oats. Hidden gluten in: soy sauce, many salad dressings, soups, marinades, processed meats, beer. Gluten-free substitutes (bread, pasta, cookies) — treat as occasional, not daily.

title: Build Muscle — Mediterranean
summary: The Mediterranean diet is excellent for muscle building — high in quality protein from fish, eggs, and legumes, rich in anti-inflammatory fats that support recovery, and carbohydrate-forward enough to fuel serious training. The focus shifts from deficit to surplus — eat more of the same quality foods.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above your TDEE. Muscle building requires a calorie surplus — without it, training stimulus goes to waste. Gain weight slowly: 0.5-1 lb per week. If gaining faster, reduce by 200 calories.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight — higher than typical Mediterranean guidance, but necessary for muscle growth. Carbs: 45-55% of calories — fuel for training. Fat: 25-30% from olive oil, fish, nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large — fuel for the day)
• 4 eggs scrambled in olive oil + 2 slices whole grain toast + ½ avocado
• OR Greek yoghurt (large — 200g) + granola (¼ cup) + banana + 2 tbsp walnuts

LUNCH (biggest meal)
• 7oz grilled chicken or tuna + 1 cup quinoa or chickpeas + large salad + olive oil dressing
• OR lentil and vegetable soup (large bowl) + 2 slices whole grain bread + side Greek yoghurt

PRE-WORKOUT SNACK
• Banana + handful of almonds + Greek yoghurt
• OR whole grain toast + 2 tbsp almond butter

DINNER
• 7oz salmon or white fish + 1 cup brown rice or pasta (whole grain) + large portion of vegetables
• OR chicken thighs + roasted vegetables + 1 cup couscous

POST-WORKOUT
• Greek yoghurt + banana + drizzle of honey
• OR protein shake if struggling to hit protein targets
portion_control: On a muscle-building plan, the goal is to eat enough — not too little. If you're not gaining weight after 2 weeks, eat 200 more calories. The Mediterranean diet is filling — you may need to eat when not fully hungry to hit your surplus.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN TARGET: Greek yoghurt, eggs, fish, and legumes at every meal. A protein shake can bridge the gap if needed.
TIMING: Eat a carb + protein meal within 1-2 hours before training and within 1 hour after. This maximises muscle protein synthesis.
SLEEP: 8 hours minimum. Muscle is built during sleep — this is not optional.
foods_to_avoid: Alcohol (significantly impairs muscle protein synthesis), excessive processed food, sugary drinks that displace nutrient-dense calories.

title: Build Muscle — Keto
summary: Building muscle on keto is possible but harder than on a higher-carb diet. Carbohydrates are the preferred fuel for intense resistance training — without them, performance may suffer. The strategy is maximising protein, keeping calories in a surplus, and accepting that muscle gain may be slower than on a standard diet.
calories: Add 200-300 calories above TDEE. Keto muscle building requires a surplus but fat gain comes faster without carbs to partition nutrients into muscle. Keep the surplus modest and monitor progress monthly.
macros: Protein: 1-1.2g per lb of bodyweight — higher than standard keto to compensate for the lack of carb-driven insulin for muscle protein synthesis. Fat: 60-65% of calories. Carbs: under 30g net — maintain ketosis.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 4 eggs scrambled in butter + 3 strips bacon + ½ avocado + handful of spinach
• OR smoked salmon (4oz) + 3 eggs + cream cheese + cucumber

LUNCH
• 7oz ground beef or chicken thigh + large salad with avocado, olive oil, cheese
• OR tuna salad (large portion) + celery + cucumber + hard boiled eggs

PRE-WORKOUT
• Hard boiled eggs (2-3) + cheese (1oz)
• OR beef jerky (no sugar) + handful of macadamia nuts

DINNER
• 8oz ribeye or salmon + roasted broccoli and cauliflower in butter + side salad
• OR lamb chops + sautéed spinach + creamy cauliflower mash with butter and cream

POST-WORKOUT
• Protein shake (whey or egg white, check for carbs) + almond milk
• OR cottage cheese (½ cup) + walnuts
portion_control: Eating enough is the challenge on keto muscle gain — fat is satiating and it is easy to under-eat. If not gaining weight, increase fat portions at each meal. Butter, olive oil, and fatty cuts of meat are your calorie-dense tools.
struggle_tips:
PERFORMANCE: Expect reduced training performance for 3-6 weeks as your body adapts to fat as fuel. Power output typically recovers but may never fully match carb-fuelled performance.
CREATINE: Supplement creatine monohydrate 5g daily — it is especially important on keto to support explosive training performance.
ELECTROLYTES: Salt, magnesium, and potassium are critical on keto — supplement them or performance and recovery suffer.
foods_to_avoid: All carbohydrates above 30g net per day, sugar, grains, fruit (except small amounts of berries), starchy vegetables, legumes.

title: Build Muscle — Carnivore
summary: Carnivore muscle building is protein-forward and simple. Animal protein is the most bioavailable protein source available — absorption rates are high and amino acid profiles are complete. The strategy is eating enough calories from animal foods to support a surplus, with protein as the primary driver.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above TDEE. Choose fattier cuts to hit the surplus — fatty ground beef (80/20), ribeye, lamb, and pork belly are your calorie-dense tools. Leaner cuts make the surplus harder to hit.
macros: Protein: 1-1.2g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: the rest of your calories. Carbs: zero. The ratio of lean to fatty protein determines your macro split — adjust fat intake by choosing leaner or fattier cuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large)
• 4-5 eggs cooked in butter + 4 strips bacon + 4oz ground beef
• OR 6oz smoked salmon + 3 eggs scrambled in butter

LUNCH
• 8oz ground beef (80/20) pan-fried + 2 hard boiled eggs + cheese (1-2oz if dairy included)
• OR chicken thighs (2 large, skin on) + 3 strips bacon

PRE-WORKOUT
• Beef jerky (no sugar) 2-3oz
• OR hard boiled eggs (2-3)

DINNER
• 10oz ribeye or NY strip cooked in butter
• OR 8oz salmon + 2 eggs scrambled
• OR lamb chops (2-3) + ground beef (4oz)

POST-WORKOUT
• Whey protein shake (2 scoops) in water — if dairy is included
• OR 3 hard boiled eggs + beef jerky
portion_control: Eat to satiety on a muscle-building carnivore plan. If not gaining weight after 2 weeks, add one extra meal or increase portion size at dinner. Organ meats (liver, heart) are nutrient-dense additions — 3-4oz of liver weekly covers most micronutrient needs.
struggle_tips:
DIGESTIVE ADAPTATION: Increased meat intake changes gut bacteria. Some people experience constipation or loose stools initially — this resolves within 2-4 weeks.
MICRONUTRIENTS: Organ meats cover most gaps. Liver once or twice weekly is strongly recommended. Some carnivore athletes supplement vitamin C — debate exists on whether this is necessary.
VARIETY: Rotate protein sources — beef, lamb, pork, poultry, and fish provide different nutrient profiles.
foods_to_avoid: Everything non-animal. All plants, grains, vegetables, fruit, and processed foods.

title: Build Muscle — Vegetarian
summary: Vegetarian muscle building is well-supported by research when protein targets are hit. Eggs and dairy are your most powerful tools — they provide complete proteins with excellent amino acid profiles. Legumes, tofu, and tempeh fill out the rest. The key is eating enough total protein across enough meals.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above TDEE. Vegetarian muscle building is calorie-manageable because eggs and dairy are calorie-dense. Focus on hitting the protein target first, then fill remaining calories with carbs and healthy fats.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight — achievable but requires deliberate planning. Carbs: 50-55% of calories — fuels training. Fat: 20-25% from eggs, dairy, olive oil, and nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large)
• 4 eggs scrambled + 1 cup cottage cheese + 2 slices whole grain toast + banana
• OR Greek yoghurt (200g) + 2 scoops protein powder (mixed in) + granola + berries

LUNCH
• Tofu stir-fry (7oz firm tofu) + 1 cup brown rice + large portion of vegetables
• OR 3-egg omelette + 1 cup lentils + large salad
• OR cottage cheese bowl (1 cup) + chickpeas (½ cup) + vegetables + olive oil

PRE-WORKOUT
• Banana + Greek yoghurt + handful of oats
• OR whole grain toast + 2 eggs + almond butter

DINNER
• Tempeh (6oz) + 1 cup quinoa + roasted vegetables + tahini sauce
• OR paneer (5oz) curry + 1 cup basmati rice + side salad
• OR egg fried rice (3 eggs + 1 cup rice + vegetables + soy sauce)

POST-WORKOUT
• Whey protein shake (2 scoops) + banana
• OR Greek yoghurt (large) + honey + granola
portion_control: On a muscle gain plan, err toward eating more rather than less. Protein is the priority — if you're hitting 1g/lb and not gaining weight, add carbs at lunch and dinner. Vegetarian muscle building sometimes requires eating when not hungry.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN DISTRIBUTION: Spread protein across 4 meals. Muscle protein synthesis is maximised with 30-40g per meal rather than all at once.
IRON: Non-haem iron from plants is less absorbed than haem iron. Eat iron-rich foods (lentils, spinach, tofu) with vitamin C. Cook in cast iron pans.
CREATINE: Vegetarians have lower baseline creatine stores — supplementing 5g daily produces significant strength and muscle gains.
foods_to_avoid: Processed vegetarian substitutes high in sodium, excessive refined carbs, sugary drinks, alcohol (impairs muscle protein synthesis).

title: Build Muscle — Vegan
summary: Vegan muscle building requires the most planning of any dietary approach but is entirely achievable. The two non-negotiables are: hitting protein targets and supplementing strategically. Without deliberate planning, vegan diets fall short on protein, B12, iron, zinc, and omega-3 — all critical for muscle growth and recovery.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above TDEE. Vegan muscle gain is helped by calorie-dense foods: nut butters, tahini, avocado, and tofu. Don't rely solely on vegetables — they won't get you to a surplus.
macros: Protein: 1-1.1g per lb of bodyweight. Carbs: 50-55% of calories. Fat: 25-30% from nuts, seeds, avocado, and oils. A plant-based protein powder is almost mandatory at this protein target.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large)
• Tofu scramble (6oz) + 2 slices whole grain toast + ½ avocado + spinach
• OR protein smoothie: 2 scoops plant protein + banana + oats (½ cup) + almond butter (1 tbsp) + almond milk

LUNCH
• Tempeh bowl (6oz) + 1 cup brown rice + roasted vegetables + tahini
• OR large lentil and chickpea salad + 2 tbsp hemp seeds + olive oil
• OR soy protein stir-fry + 1 cup noodles + vegetables

PRE-WORKOUT
• Banana + 1 tbsp almond butter + plant protein shake

DINNER

portion_control: Vegan muscle gain requires eating more than feels comfortable initially. Meals need to be large and protein-dense. If not gaining weight, add a fourth meal or increase nut butter and avocado portions.
struggle_tips:
SUPPLEMENTS (non-negotiable): B12, creatine 5g daily, omega-3 (algae-based), vitamin D, zinc. Creatine is especially impactful for vegan athletes who start with very low baseline levels.
PROTEIN QUALITY: Combine protein sources to ensure complete amino acid profiles — rice + lentils, tofu + quinoa. Leucine is the key amino acid for muscle synthesis — highest in soy, lupine, and pea protein.
TIMING: Protein immediately post-workout is more important on a vegan diet — plant proteins digest faster.
foods_to_avoid: Processed vegan junk food, sugary drinks, refined carbs that displace nutrient-dense calories, excessive alcohol.

title: Build Muscle — Paleo
summary: Paleo muscle building works well because protein quality is high and food quality is excellent. The limitation is carbohydrate availability for fuelling intense training — sweet potato, fruit, and white rice (some paleo followers include it) become important pre-workout fuel sources.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above TDEE. Paleo muscle gain means eating more meat, fish, eggs, starchy vegetables, and fruit. Sweet potato and banana become important calorie and carb sources for training fuel.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight — easily achievable on paleo. Carbs: 35-40% of calories from sweet potato, fruit, squash, and plantain. Fat: 30-35% from meat, fish, eggs, avocado, and nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large)
• 4 eggs + 4oz ground turkey or beef + sweet potato hash (1 cup) + spinach
• OR smoked salmon (5oz) + 3 eggs + avocado + sweet potato (½ cup)

LUNCH
• 7oz chicken breast or thigh + large salad + sweet potato (medium) + olive oil
• OR ground beef bowl (7oz) + cauliflower rice + roasted vegetables + avocado

PRE-WORKOUT
• Banana + almond butter (1 tbsp) + hard boiled eggs (2)
• OR sweet potato (small) + beef jerky

DINNER
• 8oz salmon or steak + roasted sweet potato + large plate of roasted vegetables
• OR chicken thighs (2) + plantain (roasted) + salad
• OR lamb + roasted beets and carrots + arugula salad

POST-WORKOUT
• Banana + egg white protein (2 scoops if using — check ingredients)
• OR 3 hard boiled eggs + apple
portion_control: Paleo muscle gain requires eating more than paleo fat loss — don't restrict. Increase sweet potato, fruit, and meat portions if not gaining weight. Nuts are calorie-dense but also easy to overeat — use them to add calories, not as a primary protein source.
struggle_tips:
CARB TIMING: Put sweet potato, fruit, and starchy vegetables around workouts — before for energy, after for glycogen replenishment.
PROTEIN VARIETY: Rotate between beef, chicken, salmon, turkey, eggs, and organ meats for the full spectrum of amino acids and micronutrients.
SLEEP: 8+ hours. Paleo's anti-inflammatory food profile supports recovery — combine with adequate sleep for best results.
foods_to_avoid: Grains, legumes, dairy, refined sugar, processed foods, seed oils, alcohol.

title: Build Muscle — Intermittent Fasting
summary: Building muscle with intermittent fasting is possible but requires compressing more food into fewer hours. The eating window needs to contain enough protein and calories to support muscle growth — this means large, nutrient-dense meals. Leangaining (lean muscle gain via IF) is the classic approach.
calories: Add 200-300 calories above TDEE, spread across your eating window. Gaining too fast on IF is easy if meals are large — monitor weekly and adjust if gaining more than 1 lb/week.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight across 2-3 meals — 40-50g per meal. Carbs: 50% of calories, timed around training. Fat: 25-30% of calories.
meals:
EATING WINDOW: 12pm – 8pm (adjust to your schedule)

MEAL 1 (12pm — largest meal, ideally around training)
• 8oz chicken breast or salmon + 1.5 cups brown rice or sweet potato + large salad
• This is your primary anabolic meal — make it count
• If training in the morning: eat this immediately post-workout

MEAL 2 (4-5pm)
• 7oz protein (any source) + 1 cup carbs + vegetables
• OR Greek yoghurt (large) + protein shake + banana + oats

MEAL 3 (7:30pm — close window)
• 7oz protein + vegetables + moderate carbs
• Keep fat moderate here — high fat slows digestion and may disrupt sleep

PRE-FAST SNACK (if still in window and needed)
• Cottage cheese (1 cup) — casein protein digests slowly and provides amino acids overnight
• OR Greek yoghurt + handful of walnuts
portion_control: Meals must be larger on IF to hit calorie and protein targets. This can be uncomfortable initially. Eat slowly and completely — skipping a meal in your window means missing growth opportunity. Liquid calories (shakes, smoothies) help when solid food feels like too much.
struggle_tips:
TRAINING TIMING: Train at the end of your fasting window or start of your eating window — this is when muscle building is most efficient. Training fasted (especially with caffeine) can work but performance may suffer.
PROTEIN PER MEAL: With only 2-3 meals, each one needs 40-50g protein. This requires deliberate planning — most people drastically underestimate how much food that is.
SLEEP: IF and good sleep are a powerful combination for growth hormone release. Don't compromise sleep to extend the fast.
foods_to_avoid: Calorie-containing drinks during fasting window, junk food that wastes precious eating window calories, alcohol (severely impairs muscle protein synthesis and disrupts IF metabolic benefits).

title: Build Muscle — Gluten-Free
summary: Gluten-free muscle building is straightforward because the best muscle-building foods are naturally gluten-free — meat, fish, eggs, rice, potatoes, vegetables, and fruit. The trap is relying on gluten-free processed products as carb sources — they're often nutrient-poor. Stick to whole foods.
calories: Add 300-400 calories above TDEE. Rice, potatoes, sweet potatoes, and gluten-free oats are your primary carb sources for fuelling training. Ensure each meal has a substantial protein source.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight. Carbs: 50% of calories from rice, potatoes, GF oats, fruit. Fat: 25% from eggs, meat, fish, avocado, olive oil.
meals:
BREAKFAST (large)
• 4 eggs scrambled + 1 cup cooked rice or GF oats + banana
• OR GF protein smoothie (2 scoops, check label) + oat milk + banana + almond butter

LUNCH
• 7oz chicken or salmon + 1.5 cups brown rice + roasted vegetables + olive oil
• OR rice noodle bowl (large) + 6oz protein + vegetables + tamari

PRE-WORKOUT
• Banana + rice cakes (3) + almond butter
• OR sweet potato (medium) + hard boiled eggs (2)

DINNER
• 8oz steak or salmon + baked potato (large) + side salad
• OR chicken thighs + quinoa (1 cup) + roasted vegetables
• OR ground turkey stir-fry + rice noodles + vegetables + tamari

POST-WORKOUT
• GF protein shake (2 scoops, verified GF) + banana
• OR Greek yoghurt (large) + rice cakes + honey
portion_control: Muscle gain requires eating enough — don't restrict carbs on training days. Rice and potato portions should be generous: 1-1.5 cups cooked rice, 1-2 medium potatoes. Increase portions if not gaining weight after 2 weeks.
struggle_tips:
LABEL CHECKING: All supplements including protein powder and creatine should be certified GF. Cross-contamination is a risk with oats — use certified GF oats.
EATING OUT: Asian restaurants are the most GF-friendly — rice-based dishes with tamari (GF soy sauce) are widely available. Confirm with staff.
CREATINE: Standard creatine monohydrate is gluten-free — take 5g daily for meaningful strength and muscle gains.
foods_to_avoid: Wheat, barley, rye, regular oats, soy sauce (use tamari), many marinades and sauces. Gluten-free processed substitutes — use whole food carbs instead.

title: Recomp — Mediterranean
summary: Body recomposition — losing fat while building muscle simultaneously — is most achievable for beginners, those returning after a break, and those with higher body fat. The Mediterranean diet is ideal for recomp because it supports both goals: adequate protein for muscle, anti-inflammatory fats for recovery, and fibre for satiety on maintenance calories.
calories: Eat at maintenance — your TDEE with no adjustment. Protein must be high to enable muscle gain while the deficit (created by protein's thermic effect and training) burns fat. Recomp is slow — expect 8-16 weeks before visible changes.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight — this is the recomp lever. Carbs: 40% of calories, timed around training. Fat: 25-30% from olive oil, fish, and nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3-4 eggs + 1 slice whole grain toast + ½ avocado + spinach
• OR Greek yoghurt (large, plain) + berries + 2 tbsp walnuts

LUNCH
• 6oz chicken or tuna + 1 cup chickpeas or quinoa + large salad + olive oil

PRE-WORKOUT
• Greek yoghurt + banana
• OR whole grain toast + almond butter

DINNER
• 6oz salmon + roasted vegetables + ½ cup brown rice
• OR chicken + large salad + small portion legumes

POST-WORKOUT
• Protein shake or Greek yoghurt + fruit
portion_control: Maintenance calories requires precision — not too much, not too little. Weigh yourself weekly. Scale should stay roughly the same while body composition shifts. If gaining weight, cut 100 calories. If losing weight rapidly, add 100 calories.
struggle_tips:
PATIENCE: Recomp changes are visible in the mirror before the scale. Trust the process for 12 weeks before reassessing.
PROTEIN TIMING: Protein at every meal and especially post-workout maximises muscle protein synthesis on maintenance calories.
SLEEP: 8 hours is non-negotiable for recomp. Growth hormone peaks during deep sleep — this is when recomp happens.
foods_to_avoid: Alcohol (kills recomp — impairs both fat loss and muscle gain), refined carbs, sugary drinks, excessive processed food.

title: Recomp — Keto
summary: Keto recomp is one of the harder combinations — carbohydrates support muscle protein synthesis, and without them, muscle gain is slower. However, keto's fat-burning efficiency can make fat loss faster, leading to a net positive recomp effect over time. Protein must be very high and training must be consistent.
calories: Eat at maintenance or 100-200 below. Keto's appetite suppression often creates a natural deficit — this is useful for recomp. Monitor weekly: if losing muscle (strength dropping), add 200 calories via fat.
macros: Protein: 1.1-1.2g per lb — higher than standard keto to compensate for reduced insulin-driven muscle synthesis. Fat: 60-65% of calories. Carbs: under 25g net.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 4 eggs + 3 strips bacon + ½ avocado + spinach in butter

LUNCH
• 6oz ground beef or chicken thigh + large salad + avocado + olive oil

PRE-WORKOUT
• Hard boiled eggs (2-3) + cheese
• OR beef jerky + macadamia nuts

DINNER
• 7oz ribeye or salmon + roasted broccoli in butter + side salad

POST-WORKOUT
• Protein shake (whey, low carb) + almond milk
• OR cottage cheese (½ cup) + walnuts
portion_control: Maintenance on keto — eat to mild satiety, not stuffed. Keto hunger signals are reliable once fat-adapted. Creatine 5g daily is essential for maintaining training performance without carbs.
struggle_tips:
STRENGTH MAINTENANCE: Strength may dip initially on keto recomp. This is normal during fat adaptation. Push through weeks 3-6 before judging performance.
ELECTROLYTES: Supplement sodium, magnesium, and potassium daily. Deficiency is the most common cause of poor performance and fatigue on keto.
CREATINE: 5g daily — critical for keto athletes.
foods_to_avoid: All carbs above 25g net, sugar, grains, starchy vegetables, most fruit, alcohol.

title: Recomp — Paleo
summary: Paleo recomp works well because food quality is high, protein is abundant, and anti-inflammatory eating supports recovery. Sweet potato, fruit, and starchy vegetables provide carbs for training without compromising the paleo framework.
calories: Maintenance calories. Sweet potato and fruit around training windows. Protein at every meal.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb of bodyweight. Carbs: 35-40% from sweet potato, fruit, and starchy vegetables. Fat: 30-35% from meat, fish, eggs, avocado, nuts.

struggle_tips:
CARB TIMING: All starchy carbs (sweet potato, plantain, fruit) go before and after training. Evenings are lower carb.
NUTS: Easy to overeat and will push you into a surplus — measure them if recomp is stalling.
SLEEP: Paleo's anti-inflammatory profile supports deep sleep. Prioritise 8 hours.
foods_to_avoid: Grains, legumes, dairy, refined sugar, seed oils, alcohol, processed paleo snacks.

title: Recomp — Vegetarian
summary: Vegetarian recomp is achievable with eggs, dairy, and plant proteins working together. Protein is the most critical variable — it must be at 1g per lb at maintenance calories to drive muscle gain while the body uses stored fat for energy.
calories: Maintenance. Protein at 1g per lb is the non-negotiable. Carbs and fat fill the remaining calories. Track for at least 2 weeks — vegetarian recomp requires precision.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb. Carbs: 45-50% timed around training. Fat: 25% from eggs, dairy, olive oil, nuts.

struggle_tips:
CREATINE: Vegetarians have 30-40% lower baseline muscle creatine. Supplementing 5g daily produces disproportionately large strength and muscle gains compared to meat eaters.
IRON: Pair plant iron sources with vitamin C. Low iron tanks energy and recovery.
PROTEIN SPREAD: 30-40g protein across 4 meals maximises muscle protein synthesis.
foods_to_avoid: Refined carbs, sugary drinks, excessive cheese (high fat, displaces protein calories), alcohol, processed vegetarian substitutes.

title: Recomp — Vegan
summary: Vegan recomp requires the most planning — protein targets are hardest to hit on maintenance calories without animal products. A plant-based protein powder is essentially mandatory. With correct supplementation and food planning, vegan recomp produces real results.
calories: Maintenance. High protein is the lever — everything else fills around it. Track rigorously for the first 4 weeks.
macros: Protein: 1-1.1g per lb — requires protein powder daily. Carbs: 50% timed around training. Fat: 20-25% from nuts, seeds, avocado.

struggle_tips:

LEUCINE: The key amino acid for muscle synthesis is lowest in plant proteins. Soy, pea, and rice protein blends are best. Leucine supplementation (2-3g per meal) can help.
TIMING: Post-workout protein within 30 minutes is more critical on plant proteins due to faster digestion.
foods_to_avoid: Processed vegan junk food, sugary drinks, refined carbs displacing protein calories, excessive oils adding empty calories, alcohol.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Mediterranean
summary: The Mediterranean diet is the most evidence-backed eating pattern for long-term health, energy, and wellbeing. At maintenance calories the goal is not restriction but optimisation — eating the best foods in the right amounts to feel and perform at your best every day.
calories: Eat at TDEE — your maintenance level. No deficit, no surplus. If energy is high and weight is stable — you're on target.
macros: Protein: 0.7-0.8g per lb. Fat: 35% from olive oil, fish, nuts, and avocado. Carbs: 45-50% from vegetables, whole grains, legumes, and fruit.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 2 eggs + 1 slice whole grain toast + ½ avocado + coffee
• OR Greek yoghurt + berries + walnuts + drizzle of honey

LUNCH

• OR lentil soup + whole grain bread + side salad

DINNER
• Grilled fish or chicken + roasted vegetables + small portion whole grain or legumes
• OR vegetable-rich pasta (whole grain, small portion) + olive oil + parmesan

SNACKS
• Fruit + handful of nuts
• Greek yoghurt
• Olives + cucumber
portion_control: Maintenance is about consistency not perfection. Eat slowly. Stop at 80% full. Allow occasional indulgences without guilt — the Mediterranean diet includes wine, good bread, and dessert in moderation. It is a lifestyle, not a diet.
struggle_tips:
ENERGY: If energy dips, increase complex carbs at lunch. If feeling heavy, reduce bread and pasta portions and increase vegetables.
SLEEP: Mediterranean eating improves sleep quality — omega-3s from fish and magnesium from vegetables and nuts are natural sleep supporters.
LONG TERM: The Mediterranean diet works because it is enjoyable. Cook with olive oil, eat with others, take time over meals.
foods_to_avoid: Ultra-processed food, sugary drinks, fast food, seed oils. Moderate red wine is acceptable — excessive alcohol is not.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Paleo
summary: Paleo maintenance is about eating whole, unprocessed foods that support energy, mood, and long-term health. At maintenance the goal is not restriction but quality — the best version of yourself fed by the best foods available.
calories: Eat at TDEE. Weight stable, energy high, sleep good — those are your metrics, not the scale.
macros: Protein: 0.7-0.8g per lb. Fat: 35-40% from meat, fish, avocado, nuts. Carbs: 30-35% from sweet potato, fruit, and vegetables.

LUNCH
• Chicken or fish + large salad + olive oil
• OR ground beef bowl + roasted vegetables + avocado

DINNER
• Steak or salmon + roasted vegetables
• OR chicken thighs + sweet potato + salad

SNACKS

• Hard boiled eggs
• Beef jerky
portion_control: Paleo maintenance is naturally self-regulating — whole foods are filling and the elimination of processed food removes the biggest sources of overconsumption. Eat when hungry, stop when full.
struggle_tips:
SOCIAL EATING: Paleo is the hardest diet to maintain socially. Plan for it — eat before events, choose grilled protein and salad at restaurants, allow occasional flexibility without it derailing the whole approach.
VARIETY: Rotate proteins and vegetables. Boredom leads to non-paleo choices.
ORGAN MEATS: Liver once a week is a micronutrient insurance policy.
foods_to_avoid: Grains, legumes, dairy, refined sugar, processed foods, seed oils.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Gluten-Free
summary: Gluten-free maintenance focuses on naturally GF whole foods for energy, health, and wellbeing. The goal is to feel your best — no bloating, good energy, stable mood — by eating clean, naturally GF foods rather than GF substitute products.
calories: Eat at TDEE. Focus on food quality over quantity.
macros: Protein: 0.7-0.8g per lb. Carbs: from rice, potatoes, GF oats, fruit. Fat: from meat, fish, eggs, olive oil, nuts.
meals:

struggle_tips:
LABEL READING: Hidden gluten is the main maintenance challenge. Keep tamari, GF soy sauce, and GF condiments stocked at home.
GF SUBSTITUTES: Occasional GF bread or pasta is fine for maintenance — just don't rely on them as daily staples.
ENERGY: If energy is low, increase complex GF carbs — rice, potatoes, oats.
foods_to_avoid: Wheat, barley, rye, regular soy sauce, many packaged sauces and dressings. Check labels on all packaged foods.

title: Recomp — Carnivore
summary: Carnivore recomp is surprisingly effective. High protein naturally supports muscle retention and growth, while zero carbs creates a metabolic environment that burns fat efficiently. The simplicity of the diet removes decision fatigue — eat animal products, train hard, sleep well.
calories: Eat at maintenance or slightly below. Protein's high thermic effect (30% of calories burned in digestion) creates a natural deficit without counting. If weight isn't moving, choose leaner cuts. If strength is dropping, add fattier cuts.
macros: Protein: 1.1-1.2g per lb of bodyweight. Fat: the remainder of your calories. Carbs: zero. Choose lean cuts (sirloin, chicken breast, white fish) on fat loss days; fattier cuts (ribeye, salmon, ground beef 80/20) on heavy training days.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 3-4 eggs scrambled in butter + 3 strips bacon
• OR 5oz ground beef + 2 eggs

LUNCH
• 6oz chicken breast or sirloin + 2 hard boiled eggs
• OR canned salmon + 3 slices deli turkey

PRE-WORKOUT

DINNER

• OR ground beef (6oz) + lamb chops (small)

POST-WORKOUT
• Whey protein shake (if dairy included)
• OR 3 hard boiled eggs
portion_control: Eat to satiety — carnivore's protein and fat combination produces strong fullness signals. On recomp, stop at satisfied rather than stuffed. If not seeing body composition changes after 4 weeks, reduce fat portions slightly by choosing leaner cuts.
struggle_tips:
ADAPTATION: The first 3 weeks are the hardest. Cravings, fatigue, and digestive changes are all normal. Push through — most people feel markedly better by week 4.
ELECTROLYTES: Salt food heavily. Add magnesium and potassium supplements. Electrolyte imbalance is the most common cause of poor adaptation.
MONITOR PROGRESS: Use progress photos and strength levels — not just the scale. Recomp shows in the mirror before the scale moves.
foods_to_avoid: All plant foods, processed foods, sugar, seed oils. If dairy is included, full-fat only — cheese and butter. Limit if fat loss stalls.

title: Recomp — Intermittent Fasting
summary: IF recomp is a well-established approach — the fasting window promotes fat oxidation and growth hormone release, while the eating window delivers enough protein and calories for muscle maintenance and growth. The key is maximising protein quality and timing within the eating window.
calories: Maintenance calories within your eating window. Do not restrict further — the fasting itself creates metabolic conditions for fat loss. Protein must be very high across your meals.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb across 2-3 meals — 35-50g per meal. Carbs: 45% of calories timed around training. Fat: 25-30%.
meals:
EATING WINDOW: 12pm-8pm (adjust as needed)

MEAL 1 (12pm — largest, ideally post-workout)
• 7oz chicken or salmon + 1 cup rice or sweet potato + large salad
• High protein, high carb — this meal drives muscle protein synthesis

MEAL 2 (4-5pm)
• 6oz protein + vegetables + moderate carbs
• OR Greek yoghurt (large) + protein shake + fruit

MEAL 3 (7:30pm)
• 6oz protein + vegetables + lower carbs
• Cottage cheese before closing window — slow digesting protein overnight

DURING FAST
• Black coffee, plain tea, sparkling water only
portion_control: Maintenance is the target — not surplus, not deficit. The fasting window handles the fat loss side. The eating window handles the muscle side. Weigh weekly — scale should be roughly stable while body composition shifts over weeks.
struggle_tips:
TRAINING TIMING: Train at the end of your fast or beginning of your eating window for best recomp results. This times the anabolic response with nutrient availability.
MORNING HUNGER: Peaks at 8-10am then drops. Black coffee kills it. Stay busy.
SLEEP: IF naturally aligns with circadian rhythm when eating window ends 2-3 hours before bed. This improves sleep quality and growth hormone release — both critical for recomp.
foods_to_avoid: Anything caloric during the fast. Junk food that wastes eating window calories. Alcohol — it impairs both fat loss and muscle synthesis.

title: Recomp — Gluten-Free
summary: Gluten-free recomp uses naturally GF whole foods as the foundation — rice, potatoes, meat, fish, eggs, and vegetables. The approach is identical to standard recomp: maintenance calories, very high protein, carbs timed around training. GF substitute products are avoided in favour of whole foods.
calories: Eat at maintenance. Protein at 1g per lb drives the recomp. Weigh weekly — stable weight with changing body composition is the goal.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb. Carbs: 45% from rice, potatoes, GF oats, fruit. Fat: 25-30% from meat, fish, eggs, olive oil.

struggle_tips:
LABEL CHECK: Protein powders and supplements should be certified GF. Cross-contamination risk is real for those with coeliac disease.
CARB TIMING: All GF carbs around training. Evenings lean toward protein and vegetables.
PROGRESS: Track with photos and tape measure — recomp shows in measurements before the scale.
foods_to_avoid: All gluten-containing foods. GF processed substitutes — use whole food carb sources. Regular soy sauce — use tamari.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Carnivore
summary: Carnivore maintenance is the simplest eating plan available — eat animal products, feel good, stay strong. No tracking, no measuring, no decisions. For those who thrive on carnivore, maintenance means continuing to eat this way while optimising for energy, sleep, and performance.
calories: Eat to satiety. Carnivore is self-regulating — protein and fat together produce strong fullness signals. Weight stable, energy high, mood good — those are your metrics.
macros: Protein: 0.8-1g per lb. Fat: the rest of your calories. Carbs: zero. Rotate between lean and fatty cuts based on hunger and energy.

• OR ground beef + eggs

LUNCH
• Chicken, beef, or fish + hard boiled eggs

SNACKS (only if genuinely hungry)

portion_control: Eat when hungry, stop when full. This is the entirety of portion control on carnivore maintenance. Trust your appetite — it becomes reliable after the initial adaptation period.
struggle_tips:
ORGAN MEATS: Liver once or twice weekly is a micronutrient powerhouse. Covers most gaps that a nose-to-tail carnivore approach provides.
VARIETY: Rotate protein sources — beef, pork, lamb, poultry, and fish for different nutrient profiles.
SLEEP: Many carnivore adherents report improved sleep quality. Prioritise 7-9 hours.
foods_to_avoid: All plant foods, processed meats with additives or sugar, seed oils. Keep it simple — if it came from an animal, it's in. If it didn't, it's out.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Keto
summary: Keto maintenance is about sustaining the metabolic state of ketosis while eating enough to fuel your life and training. The goal is steady energy, mental clarity, and stable weight — the hallmarks of well-maintained ketosis.
calories: Eat at TDEE. Keto maintenance is naturally self-regulating once fat-adapted. Hunger signals are reliable — eat when hungry, stop when full.
macros: Fat: 65-70% of calories. Protein: 0.7-0.8g per lb. Carbs: under 30g net daily — maintain ketosis.

portion_control: Maintenance on keto is self-regulating — eat to mild satiety. Fat is filling. If weight creeps up, reduce fat portions slightly. If energy drops, increase fat.
struggle_tips:
KETOSIS CHECKS: If energy or mental clarity drops, check carb intake — hidden carbs in sauces, dressings, and condiments are the most common culprit.
ELECTROLYTES: Maintain sodium, magnesium, and potassium supplementation long-term on keto. Deficiency causes fatigue and cramps.
SOCIAL EATING: Steak and salad, burger without bun, grilled fish and vegetables — keto is manageable at most restaurants.
foods_to_avoid: All carbs above 30g net daily. Sugar, grains, most fruit, legumes, starchy vegetables, beer, low-fat dairy products.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Vegetarian
summary: Vegetarian maintenance is about eating a varied, nutrient-rich plant-based diet with eggs and dairy providing complete proteins. The goal is sustained energy, good mood, and long-term health. Variety is the main tool — rotating vegetables, legumes, grains, and protein sources covers all nutritional bases.
calories: Eat at TDEE. Balanced plates of protein, complex carbs, healthy fats, and plenty of vegetables.
macros: Protein: 0.7g per lb from eggs, dairy, legumes, and tofu. Carbs: 50% from whole grains, legumes, and vegetables. Fat: 25% from eggs, dairy, olive oil, nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• 2-3 eggs + whole grain toast + fruit
• OR Greek yoghurt + granola + berries

LUNCH
• Large salad + chickpeas or lentils + feta + olive oil
• OR tofu or tempeh stir-fry + brown rice

DINNER
• Pasta (whole grain) + tomato sauce + vegetables + parmesan
• OR vegetable curry + chickpeas + basmati rice
• OR frittata + side salad

SNACKS
• Fruit + nuts
• Greek yoghurt
• Hummus + vegetables
portion_control: No restriction needed at maintenance — eat balanced portions and listen to hunger. The high fibre content of a vegetarian diet naturally prevents overeating.
struggle_tips:
IRON AND B12: Vegetarians are at risk of low iron and B12. Eat iron-rich foods (lentils, spinach, tofu) with vitamin C. Consider B12 supplementation.
PROTEIN VARIETY: Rotate protein sources — eggs, cottage cheese, Greek yoghurt, tofu, tempeh, lentils, chickpeas — for complete amino acid coverage.
MEAL PREP: Batch cook grains and legumes at the start of the week for easy assembly.
foods_to_avoid: Highly processed vegetarian substitutes as daily staples, refined carbs, excessive sugar, alcohol.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Vegan
summary: Vegan maintenance prioritises food variety and nutrient density to cover all bases without animal products. The focus is on feeling good — steady energy, good digestion, strong immunity. Supplementation is essential long-term on a vegan diet.
calories: Eat at TDEE. Varied whole plant foods at maintenance. No restriction — focus on quality and variety.
macros: Protein: 0.7g per lb from tofu, tempeh, legumes, and plant protein. Carbs: 55% from whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruit. Fat: 25% from nuts, seeds, avocado, olive oil.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Tofu scramble + whole grain toast + spinach
• OR smoothie: banana + spinach + plant protein + almond milk + flaxseed
• OR oats + almond milk + banana + hemp seeds

LUNCH
• Large salad + chickpeas + tahini + whole grain pita
• OR lentil soup + rye bread
• OR tempeh bowl + brown rice + roasted vegetables

DINNER
• Tofu or seitan stir-fry + noodles or rice
• OR black bean tacos + corn tortillas + avocado + salsa
• OR vegetable and lentil curry + basmati rice

SNACKS
• Fruit + almond butter
• Edamame
• Hummus + vegetables
• Trail mix (nuts + seeds + dried fruit)
portion_control: Eat to hunger at maintenance. Vegan diets are high in fibre and volume — satiety is generally good. Watch calorie-dense foods like nuts, nut butters, and oils — easy to overeat.
struggle_tips:
SUPPLEMENTS (non-negotiable long-term): B12, vitamin D, omega-3 (algae-based), iodine, zinc, and iron if tested low. These are not optional on a vegan diet — deficiency develops slowly and silently.
VARIETY: The wider the variety of plants, the better the micronutrient coverage. Aim for 30 different plants per week.
SOCIAL EATING: Thai, Indian, Ethiopian, and Middle Eastern cuisines offer excellent vegan options. Plan ahead.
foods_to_avoid: All animal products, processed vegan junk food as daily staples, refined sugar, excessive oils.

title: Maintain and Feel Better — Intermittent Fasting
summary: IF maintenance uses the eating window to deliver a day's worth of balanced nutrition while allowing the fasting window to support metabolic health, mental clarity, and cellular repair. The goal is steady energy, good focus, and stable weight — not restriction.
calories: Eat at TDEE within your eating window. 2-3 complete meals. No snacking outside the window.
macros: Protein: 0.7-0.8g per lb across meals. Carbs: 45-50%. Fat: 30%. Balanced across each meal.
meals:
EATING WINDOW EXAMPLE: 12pm-8pm

MEAL 1 (12pm)
• Complete meal: protein + carbs + vegetables + healthy fat
• Grilled chicken + rice + salad + olive oil
• OR eggs + sweet potato + vegetables

MEAL 2 (4-5pm)
• Moderate sized meal: protein + vegetables + smaller carb portion
• OR Greek yoghurt + fruit + nuts as a bridge meal

MEAL 3 (7:30pm)
• Complete dinner: protein + vegetables + healthy fat
• Lower in carbs than Meal 1 — you're winding down

DURING FAST
• Black coffee, plain tea, sparkling water
portion_control: With a compressed eating window, each meal should be satisfying — not restrictive. Eat slowly and fully. Skipping meals within the window creates unnecessary restriction and hunger.
struggle_tips:
CONSISTENCY: The biggest benefit of IF comes from doing it consistently most days. Occasional flexibility is fine — don't let one off day become a week.
MORNING ROUTINE: Build a non-food morning routine — exercise, meditation, reading, coffee. Keeping busy makes the fast easy.
SLEEP: IF aligns naturally with good sleep hygiene when the eating window closes 2-3 hours before bed.
foods_to_avoid: Calorie-containing foods and drinks during the fasting window. Junk food during the eating window — with fewer meals, every one counts.

title: Fat Loss — Mediterranean (Eating Out)
summary: Mediterranean fat loss when you eat out most of the time. Restaurant eating doesn't have to derail fat loss — it requires knowing what to order, how to modify dishes, and where hidden calories live. This plan gives you the framework for eating Mediterranean at any restaurant.
calories: Subtract 400 calories from TDEE. Restaurant portions are typically 30-50% larger than home portions — visually split the plate and take half home, or order a starter as your main.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb — order protein first. Fat: 30-35% — olive oil dressing, avocado, fish. Carbs: from vegetables, legumes, and small amounts of whole grains.
meals:
BREAKFAST (café or home)
• Eggs any style + side salad or avocado — ask for no toast or one slice
• OR Greek yoghurt + fruit (most cafes have this)
• Black coffee

LUNCH (restaurant)
• Grilled fish or chicken + side salad + vegetables — ask for dressing on the side
• Greek salad + grilled protein added
• Avoid: pasta dishes, pizza, bread baskets
• Ask for: olive oil instead of butter, dressing on the side, extra vegetables instead of fries

DINNER (restaurant)
• Grilled salmon, sea bass, or chicken + roasted vegetables
• Share a starter of hummus or olives instead of ordering your own
• One glass of wine maximum — or skip
• Avoid: creamy sauces, fried dishes, large pasta portions

SNACKS (on the go)
• Nuts (pre-portioned 1oz bag)
• Greek yoghurt from a café
• Apple + string cheese
portion_control: The 50% rule: when a restaurant plate arrives, visually identify half and mentally commit to stopping there. Ask for a box immediately if it helps. Never eat bread before the meal — 200 hidden calories before the main arrives.
struggle_tips:
ORDERING STRATEGY: Protein + vegetables + salad is available at virtually every restaurant. Ask confidently — staff are used to modifications.
HIDDEN CALORIES: Dressings (200-400 cal), sauces, bread, and cooking oils are the main culprits. Ask for sauces on the side always.
ALCOHOL: Each glass of wine is 120-150 calories and lowers inhibition around food choices. Limit or skip on fat loss phase.
foods_to_avoid: Bread baskets, creamy pasta, fried dishes, sugary cocktails, desserts, anything described as crispy, battered, or smothered.

title: Fat Loss — Keto (Eating Out)
summary: Keto eating out is manageable once you know the rules. Almost every restaurant has a keto-compatible option — it just requires knowing how to order and what to avoid. The three pillars: protein, fat, and zero hidden carbs in sauces or dressings.
calories: 400-500 below TDEE. Restaurant portions of protein and fat are usually generous — portion control matters less than carb avoidance on keto eating out.
macros: Fat: 65-70%. Protein: 0.85g per lb. Carbs: under 25g net — this is the non-negotiable.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Eggs (any style) + bacon + avocado — skip toast, ask for extra eggs instead
• OR smoked salmon + cream cheese + cucumber (most hotel buffets have this)

LUNCH
• Burger without the bun — most places will do a lettuce wrap
• Steak salad with olive oil dressing
• Grilled chicken + side salad, no croutons, dressing on side
• Avoid: wraps, sandwiches, anything in a bun, soups with unknown ingredients

DINNER
• Steak + side salad + steamed vegetables (ask for butter not oil)
• Grilled fish + roasted vegetables, ask for no sauce or sauce on side
• Ask to substitute: fries → side salad; rice → extra vegetables

SNACKS
• Hard boiled eggs (keep in bag)
• Cheese from a deli
• Nuts (1oz pre-portioned)
• Deli meat roll-ups
portion_control: Protein portions at restaurants are usually 6-10oz — appropriate for keto. Fat is filling — don't add extra. The main portion control issue on keto eating out is hidden carbs in sauces derailing ketosis, not overeating.
struggle_tips:
SAUCE VIGILANCE: Most restaurant sauces contain sugar or starch. Always ask for sauce on the side or skip entirely. Use olive oil and lemon instead.
ASIAN RESTAURANTS: Soy sauce has carbs — ask for no sauce or bring your own tamari packet. Rice dishes can be ordered without rice.
FAST FOOD KETO: Burger patty + cheese + lettuce + tomato works at most chains. Avoid diet sodas — they can trigger insulin response.
foods_to_avoid: All bread, rice, pasta, potatoes, sugary sauces, sweetened dressings, beer, most cocktails, desserts, anything breaded or battered.

title: Fat Loss — Vegan (Eating Out)
summary: Vegan fat loss while eating out is the most challenging combination — hidden animal products, limited protein options, and high-carb defaults are everywhere. But with the right restaurant choices and ordering strategy, it is manageable.
calories: 300-400 below TDEE. Vegan restaurant options skew carb-heavy — actively seek protein at every meal to avoid fat loss plateaus from inadequate protein.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb — hardest to hit while eating out vegan. Prioritise tofu, tempeh, edamame, and legume-based dishes. Carbs: 45% from whole sources. Fat: 20-25%.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Smoothie bowl (check for honey) + extra seeds or nuts
• Avocado toast on whole grain (ask for no butter) + fruit
• Oatmeal with almond milk + banana + flaxseed

LUNCH
• Thai restaurant: tofu stir-fry with vegetables + brown rice (small) — ask for no fish sauce, no egg
• Indian: dal (lentil) + vegetable curry + small naan or rice — avoid paneer and ghee
• Salad bar: load with chickpeas, edamame, lentils, seeds — light dressing
• Mexican: bean tacos + salsa + guacamole (small) — corn tortillas, skip sour cream and cheese

DINNER
• Sushi: edamame + vegetable rolls + miso soup — ask for no mayo
• Italian: pasta e fagioli or tomato-based pasta (moderate portion) + side salad
• Middle Eastern: falafel + tabbouleh + hummus (small) + salad

SNACKS
• Edamame at Japanese restaurants
• Fruit from a café
• Nuts (pre-portioned)
portion_control: Vegan restaurant options often come in large carb-forward portions. Eat half of grain-based dishes and supplement with extra salad or vegetables. Hummus and guacamole are healthy but calorie-dense — small portions only.
struggle_tips:
BEST CUISINES: Thai, Indian, Japanese, Middle Eastern, and Mexican offer the most vegan protein options when eating out.
HIDDEN ANIMAL PRODUCTS: Fish sauce in Thai, ghee in Indian, egg in pasta — always ask. Most restaurants are used to this.
PROTEIN CHALLENGE: If struggling to hit protein eating out, keep a vegan protein bar in your bag as backup.
foods_to_avoid: Fried foods, large grain portions without protein, sugary sauces, vegan desserts, alcohol, creamy vegan dishes (often high in coconut cream or oils).

title: Build Muscle — Mediterranean (Eating Out)
summary: Building muscle while eating out on a Mediterranean diet is genuinely straightforward — grilled protein, olive oil, vegetables, and whole grains are available almost everywhere. The challenge is eating enough volume to support a surplus when restaurant portions are unpredictable.
calories: 300-400 above TDEE. Restaurant meals can be large or small — if a meal feels small, order a side of protein or an extra starter. Never leave a meal feeling like you didn't eat enough on a muscle gain plan.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb — order protein first and build around it. Carbs: 50% from grains, legumes, and vegetables. Fat: 25-30% from olive oil, fish, nuts.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Large egg dish — omelette with vegetables + 2 slices whole grain toast + fruit
• OR Greek yoghurt (large) + granola + berries + side of eggs

LUNCH
• Grilled fish or chicken + large grain salad (tabbouleh, grain bowl) + extra bread
• Greek salad + grilled protein + pita bread
• Ask for extra protein portion — most restaurants will add 2oz more for a small charge

PRE-WORKOUT SNACK
• Banana + packet of nuts + Greek yoghurt cup (grab and go)

DINNER
• Grilled salmon or sea bass + pasta or rice side + roasted vegetables + bread
• Lamb or chicken + rice or couscous + side salad
• Don't skip the bread — it contributes to the surplus

POST-WORKOUT
• Greek yoghurt + banana + nuts (if still within eating window)
• OR protein shake blended at home before or after restaurant visit
portion_control: On muscle gain, finish your plate and consider ordering sides. Restaurant bread, rice, and pasta portions are your calorie surplus tools — use them intentionally.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN FIRST: When ordering, identify the protein source and confirm the portion is adequate. A 4oz chicken breast won't build much muscle — ask for the 8oz.
SUPPLEMENT AROUND EATING OUT: A protein shake before or after a restaurant meal bridges the gap when the protein content is uncertain.
CONSISTENCY: Eating out every day on a muscle gain plan is possible but harder — one home-cooked meal prep day per week makes the rest of the week easier.
foods_to_avoid: Alcohol (impairs muscle protein synthesis), very low protein meals that waste your surplus on empty calories, excessive fried food.

title: Fat Loss — Vegetarian (Eating Out)
summary: Vegetarian fat loss while eating out requires actively seeking protein-rich options and avoiding the carb-heavy vegetarian defaults most restaurants offer. Knowing which cuisines support your goals makes eating out much easier.
calories: 400 below TDEE. Track loosely — restaurant meals are hard to measure precisely. Prioritise protein and vegetables. Keep carb portions to half the plate.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb from eggs, dairy, tofu, and legumes. Carbs: 40% — half what restaurants typically serve. Fat: 25-30%.
meals:
BREAKFAST
• Omelette (2-3 eggs) + vegetables + feta — skip the toast or have one slice
• OR Greek yoghurt parfait + fruit — ask for no granola if watching calories

LUNCH
• Indian: dal + vegetable curry + raita (yoghurt) — skip naan or have half
• Mexican: bean and cheese burrito bowl (no rice) + salsa + guacamole (small)
• Salad bar: eggs + cheese + legumes + lots of vegetables + light dressing
• Italian: caprese salad + minestrone soup + side salad — avoid pasta mains

DINNER
• Vegetable stir-fry with tofu + half portion rice
• Vegetarian sushi: avocado rolls + edamame + miso soup
• Greek: spanakopita (small) + large salad + tzatziki

SNACKS
• Greek yoghurt cup
• String cheese + apple
• Hard boiled eggs (keep in bag)
portion_control: Restaurant vegetarian dishes trend toward carbs — pasta, pizza, grain bowls. Always ask for extra protein and reduce the carb portion to half. Load up on any available salad or vegetable sides.
struggle_tips:
BEST CUISINES: Indian (dal, paneer, raita), Greek (eggs, feta, legumes), Japanese (edamame, egg dishes), Mexican (beans, eggs).
PROTEIN GAP: If a meal has no clear protein source, add a side of eggs, cheese, or yoghurt.
DRESSINGS: Ask for dressing on the side — restaurant dressings are often 200-300 extra calories.
foods_to_avoid: Bread baskets, creamy pasta, fried vegetarian options, sugary drinks, desserts, excessive cheese portions.

title: Fat Loss — Mediterranean (Meal Prep)
summary: Mediterranean fat loss built around Sunday meal prep. Four hours on Sunday produces five days of lunches and dinners, removing daily food decisions and making the deficit automatic. Consistency is the biggest driver of fat loss — meal prep is the biggest driver of consistency.
calories: 400 below TDEE. Meal prep makes this precise — you know exactly what's in every container.
macros: Protein: 0.8g per lb. Fat: 30% from olive oil, fish, nuts. Carbs: 40-45% from legumes, vegetables, whole grains.
meals:
SUNDAY PREP (4 hours):
• Cook 2 lbs chicken breast — bake at 400°F with olive oil, lemon, herbs. Slice and store.
• Cook 1 batch brown rice or quinoa (2 cups dry)
• Hard boil 10-12 eggs
• Roast 3 trays of mixed vegetables (peppers, zucchini, broccoli, eggplant) with olive oil
• Make 1 large batch of lentil soup or chickpea stew
• Pre-wash and portion salad greens into containers

DAILY MEALS:
BREAKFAST (5 min assembly)
• 2 hard boiled eggs + Greek yoghurt + berries

LUNCH (grab from fridge)
• Container: chicken breast (5oz) + ½ cup quinoa + roasted vegetables + olive oil + lemon

DINNER (10 min assembly)
• Lentil soup (reheated) + side salad + 1 slice whole grain bread
• OR fresh salmon (10 min to cook) + prepped roasted vegetables + quinoa

SNACKS (pre-portioned)
• 1oz nuts in small bags
• Greek yoghurt cups
• Pre-cut vegetables + 2 tbsp hummus
portion_control: Pre-portioning is the ultimate portion control tool. Build containers Sunday with exact portions — 5oz protein, ½ cup grains, 1 cup vegetables, 1 tbsp olive oil. No guessing Monday through Friday.
struggle_tips:
VARIETY: Rotate 2-3 protein sources each week (chicken, fish, legumes) so meal prep doesn't get boring.
FRESH ELEMENTS: Add fresh elements daily — different herbs, a squeeze of lemon, a different sauce — to keep prepped meals feeling new.
FRIDAY FLEXIBILITY: Save Friday dinner for a restaurant or takeaway within your plan — built-in flexibility prevents weekend derailment.
foods_to_avoid: Same as standard Mediterranean fat loss — avoid refined carbs, sugary dressings, processed foods, and alcohol.

title: Fat Loss — Keto (Meal Prep)
summary: Keto meal prep removes the biggest challenge of keto eating — avoiding hidden carbs in convenience food. When food is prepared in advance, staying under 25g net carbs is automatic. Sunday prep powers the entire week.
calories: 400-500 below TDEE. Prepped keto meals are naturally calorie-controlled — protein and fat satiate without the need for calorie-dense carbs.
macros: Fat: 65-70%. Protein: 0.85g per lb. Carbs: under 25g net daily.
meals:
SUNDAY PREP:
• Cook 2 lbs ground beef — season with salt, pepper, garlic. Store in portions.
• Bake 2 lbs chicken thighs (skin on) — olive oil, salt, herbs
• Hard boil 12 eggs
• Roast 3 trays low-carb vegetables: broccoli, cauliflower, zucchini, peppers in butter or olive oil
• Make cauliflower rice (1 large head, riced and sautéed in butter)
• Pre-portion nuts into 1oz bags

DAILY MEALS:
BREAKFAST
• 3 prepped hard boiled eggs + reheated bacon (cook a batch Sunday) + ½ avocado

LUNCH
• Container: ground beef or chicken thigh (5-6oz) + roasted vegetables + avocado

DINNER
• Fresh protein cooked quickly (steak, salmon, eggs — all under 15 min) + cauliflower rice + side salad
• OR reheated chicken thigh + roasted vegetables + olive oil

SNACKS
• Pre-portioned nuts (1oz bags)
• String cheese
• Hard boiled egg
portion_control: Pre-portioned containers remove all decisions. Each lunch container: 5-6oz protein, 1.5 cups roasted vegetables, ½ avocado. Everything measured Sunday.
struggle_tips:
FRESHNESS: Roasted vegetables keep 4-5 days in the fridge. Cooked ground beef keeps 4 days. Cook half the chicken Sunday, half Wednesday for freshness.
SAUCES: Make a batch of keto-friendly sauce Sunday — garlic butter, pesto (no pine nuts), or tahini — to vary flavour across the week.
FAT SOURCES: Avocado, cheese, and olive oil are easy to add fresh daily to prepped meals.
foods_to_avoid: All carbs above 25g net. Any sauce or seasoning blend with hidden sugars or starches. Processed keto products — bars, cookies — that displace real food.

title: Build Muscle — Vegan (Meal Prep)
summary: Vegan muscle gain meal prep is essential — hitting 1g protein per lb of bodyweight from plant sources requires planning. Sunday prep builds high-protein, calorie-sufficient meals for the entire week and removes the daily struggle of finding enough vegan protein.
calories: 300-400 above TDEE. Each prepped meal needs to be substantial — vegan muscle gain requires volume.
macros: Protein: 1g per lb — a protein powder is part of this plan. Carbs: 50-55%. Fat: 20-25%.
meals:
SUNDAY PREP:
• Press and bake 2 blocks firm tofu (400°F, 25 min, cubed with tamari and sesame oil)
• Cook 2 blocks tempeh — slice and pan-fry with soy sauce and garlic
• Cook 3 cups dry lentils or 2 cans each chickpeas and black beans
• Cook 4 cups dry brown rice or quinoa
• Roast 3 trays vegetables — broccoli, sweet potato, peppers, cauliflower
• Mix 5 plant protein shakes into individual mason jars (dry — add liquid daily)

DAILY MEALS:
BREAKFAST (5 min)
• Overnight oats (prepped Sunday): oats + almond milk + banana + 2 tbsp hemp seeds + plant protein scoop

LUNCH (grab from fridge)
• Container: tempeh or tofu (6oz) + ½ cup quinoa + roasted vegetables + tahini

PRE-WORKOUT
• Plant protein shake + banana

DINNER (10 min)
• Large lentil or chickpea bowl + ½ cup brown rice + fresh avocado + hot sauce
• OR tofu stir-fry with prepped vegetables + fresh noodles (10 min cook)

POST-WORKOUT
• Plant protein shake + oat milk + banana
portion_control: Muscle gain means eating full portions — don't under-fill containers. Each meal: 6oz protein source, 1 cup grains, generous vegetables, sauce. If not gaining weight after 2 weeks, increase grain and nut butter portions.
struggle_tips:
PROTEIN POWDER: Essential for vegan muscle meal prep. A pea/rice blend provides the best amino acid profile. Add to smoothies, oats, and shakes.
CREATINE: 5g daily — mix into your morning oats or protein shake. The single most impactful supplement for vegan athletes.
VARIETY: Alternate tofu and tempeh week to week. Swap quinoa for brown rice. Change the roasted vegetables. Keeps prep meals from getting monotonous.
foods_to_avoid: Processed vegan substitutes as primary protein sources, refined carbs displacing nutrient-dense calories, excessive oils adding empty calories, alcohol.
